content: The Guidelines Development Committee consisted of Jeong-Sik Byeon, Soon Man Yoon, Yunho Jung, Jong Wook Kim, and Min Seob Kwak. These individuals were responsible for the overall planning and methodology selection for the development of the guidelines. They also oversaw the detailed processes of evidence search, selection, and appraisal, provided advisory roles to the Taskforce Committee, and reviewed the development process. Additionally, they strategized the distribution and implementation of the guidelines. The Taskforce Committee included members from the Korean Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (Sun-Jin Boo, Eun Hye Oh, Seong Ran Jeon, and Seung-Joo Nam), the Korean Society of Gastroenterology (Seon-Young Park and Su Young Kim), and the Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases (Soo-kyung Park, Jaeyoung Chun, and Dong Hoon Baek). This committee was primarily responsible for sharing the development plan, collating opinions, and adapting the guidelines. They identified high-priority areas and issues for inclusion in the guidelines and determined key questions based on the scope of the guideline development. The methodology for guideline development followed a structured process. In the planning stage, key themes were selected, existing guidelines were reviewed, a development plan was established, and key questions were identified. During the development stage, evidence was searched, assessed for quality, synthesized, and used to write recommendations with determined strengths. Consensus was then drawn. In the finalization stage, external reviews were conducted, and the finalized guidelines were published. All contributors disclosed their competing interests. None of the members, including the chairperson, had prior experience with the development or approval of similar guidelines or relationships with companies related to the medicines, commodities, or services discussed in the guidelines within the two years preceding their development. Members who received research grants abstained from discussions and voting when medications from the applicable companies were considered. Financial support for the development of the guidelines was solely provided by the Korean Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy, the Korean Society of Gastroenterology, and the Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases. The guidelines were developed to provide standardized protocols for post-polypectomy colonoscopic surveillance. They aim to assist clinicians performing colonoscopies and treating patients who have undergone colorectal polyp resection. The target population includes all patients, regardless of gender or comorbidities, who have had polyps removed via colonoscopy. The intended users are clinicians, government officials, patients, and the general public. The guideline development process involved reviewing three major international guidelines: the 2020 US Multi-Society Task Force on Colorectal Cancer (USMSTF) recommendations, the 2020 British Society of Gastroenterology/Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland/Public Health England (BSG-ACGBI) guidelines, and the 2020 European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) guidelines. Twelve key questions were identified, focusing on risk factors for colorectal cancer and the optimal timing and intervals for colonoscopic surveillance. These questions addressed factors such as the size, number, and histology of adenomas and serrated polyps, as well as family history and resection methods. A systematic search for existing guidelines was conducted using international databases such as MEDLINE, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library. Guidelines were selected based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, including adherence to PICO (Patient, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome) criteria, evidence-based methodology, peer review, and publication in Korean or English since 2015. The selection process involved two rounds of screening, with disagreements resolved through discussion. Three guidelines were ultimately selected. The selected guidelines underwent appraisal using the Korean Appraisal of Guidelines for Research & Evaluation (K-AGREE) tool, which evaluates six domains: Scope and Purpose, Stakeholder Involvement, Rigor of Development, Clarity of Presentation, Applicability, and Editorial Independence. Guidelines with a standardized score of at least 50% in the Rigor of Development domain were selected, although exceptions were made for guidelines with low scores if deemed necessary by the Taskforce Committee. The Taskforce Committee summarized recommendations and evidence for each key question, comparing the content and strengths of the recommendations across the three selected guidelines. The evidence supporting each recommendation was outlined, and a draft of the statements was written based on the comprehensive level of evidence for each key question. The modified Delphi technique was used to achieve consensus among panelists, which included experts from various relevant organizations. Recommendations were adopted if at least two-thirds of the panelists agreed. Following two rounds of voting, consensus was reached on 12 recommendations. The final statements were prepared after an external review by eight colonoscopy specialists and experts who were not directly involved in the guideline development. The finalized guidelines were confirmed after a final review by the Guidelines Development Committee. The search and selection process for guidelines involved a comprehensive search strategy using terms related to patients and guidelines. A total of 590 articles were initially identified, with 503 remaining after duplicates were removed. Fifty-five articles were selected after the first screening, and three guidelines were ultimately chosen after the second screening. The selection process is detailed in a flowchart provided in Appendix 9. The appraisal process confirmed the selection of the three guidelines: the 2020 USMSTF recommendations, the 2020 BSG-ACGBI guidelines, and the 2020 ESGE guidelines. These guidelines were evaluated for their acceptability and applicability, with evidence tables and comparisons provided for each key question. The final recommendations and evidence summaries are documented in the appendices.
